claims.text: Replacing high-thermal-load LPBF with room-temperature ink extrusion followed by controlled sintering will reduce residual stress and mechanical-property degradation in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock has a typical particle-size distribution and can be produced by gas atomization or a similar method.
The starting AlCrFeNiSi powder contains no pre-induced residual stresses.
AlCrFeNiSi powder-loaded ink can be extrusion-printed into green parts at room temperature.
Sintering under inert gas or vacuum at 1200–1400 °C can consolidate extrusion-printed AlCrFeNiSi parts.
The required sintering consolidation can be achieved in a short duration.
The proposed route is applicable to miniature geometries with critical dimensions below 1 mm.
The proposed route produces a refined and thermally uniform microstructure.
Reduced exposure to high thermal gradients minimizes grain coarsening.
The proposed route produces a homogeneous phase distribution.
Laser-based melting imposes extreme thermal gradients that promote rapid solidification and thermal shock.
Room-temperature ink extrusion avoids the extreme thermal gradients and rapid solidification associated with laser melting.
Gradual consolidation during low-temperature sintering reduces the formation of residual stresses.
Gradual sintering preserves the alloy's inherent mechanical properties.
Printed-and-sintered AlCrFeNiSi parts will have significantly lower residual stresses than LPBF parts.
Printed-and-sintered AlCrFeNiSi parts will have fewer microstructural defects than LPBF parts.
Printed-and-sintered AlCrFeNiSi parts will have greater toughness and strength than LPBF parts.
Conventional LPBF creates residual thermal stresses, microstructural degradation, and complex post-processing requirements.
The proposed route may be less advantageous for larger structures because sintering-induced densification challenges become more prominent.
Optimization of the sintering profile and ink formulation is critical to obtaining the predicted benefits.
